after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Determine the entry ${a}_{12}^{′}$ in the inverse of a matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(A)=|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| & =1|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|-(-2)|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|+4|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(6-0)+2(0+1)+4(0+3) \\  & =6+2+12 \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since we want the entry ${a}_{12}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{21}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{21} & =(-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(-4-0) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{12}^{′}=\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{21}=\frac{1}{20}\cdot 4=\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Determine the entry ${a}_{31}^{′}$ in the inverse of a matrix $A$ $=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}A=|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =(-1)|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|+0|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(2+1)-(1-2)+0 \\  & =-3+1+0 \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since we want the entry ${a}_{31}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{13}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{13} & =(-1)^{1+3}|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-1-4 \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{31}^{′}=\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{13}=\frac{1}{-2}\cdot (-5)=\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Determine the entry ${a}_{31}^{′}$ in the inverse of a matrix $A$ $=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}A=|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =(-1)|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|+0|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(2+1)-(1-2)+0 \\  & =-3+1+0 \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since we want the entry ${a}_{31}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{13}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{13} & =(-1)^{1+3}|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-1-4 \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{31}^{′}=\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{13}=\frac{1}{-2}\cdot (-5)=\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
